name: PINOCHLE DOUBLE DECK
description: Partnership trick-and-meld game for four players using two 40-card pinochle packs (80 cards, nines removed). Bid to name trump, meld for points, then play 20 tricks; first team to reach the target score (e.g. 1500) wins.

content.text: Partnership trick-and-meld game for four players using two 40-card pinochle packs (80 cards, nines removed). Bid to name trump, meld for points, then play 20 tricks; first team to reach the target score (e.g. 1500) wins.

Pinochle descends from the European games bezique and Binokel. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where it was mispronounced and spelled as pinochle; it became popular among American Jewish and Irish immigrant communities. The double-deck variant uses two 40-card pinochle packs (80 cards total, nines removed) for four-player partnership play, with hand sizes and minimum bids scaled up; it shares this American cultural origin and was likewise temporarily banned in some US cities during World War I due to anti-German sentiment, before regaining popularity.
Four players in two partnerships; partners sit opposite.
All 80 cards dealt, 20 per player; typically in packets of four or five, clockwise from left of dealer.
